a19ef4e33e53323aa.summary: Method 2 is a clean, small module (engine/plant/src/dcf.rs, 528 lines). It prices two plants of equal H2 on whole-year flows at 8% real. Year 0 is the end of construction, and the reactor spends in six buckets at years -5 to 0 (CONSTRUCTION_YEARS 5.5, part year first). Interest during construction (IDC) has no line of its own: it appears only because negative years compound forward at the same rate. Today the DCF and the L5 ledger agree within 0.47% of L5 at every one of 72 points, against a stated limit of 10%. That agreement is close to a tautology, because both methods start from one CostItems set and one rate. The 10% limit therefore cannot catch a grant or IDC error that both methods share. There is no grant model. The only co-funding is a reactor-capital multiplier, rx_mult, that also shrinks IDC. Figures below come from the committed results/Economic_Ledger.csv. I did not run cargo. I reproduced the 25 y and 60 y reactor-term gaps in Python to 4 decimals.

items.finding: Year 0 is the end of construction, flows fall at year ends, and operation runs from year 1 to the horizon. discount(rate, year: i32) is (1+r)^-year, so negative years compound forward. All flows are real. Years are i32, so -5.5 cannot be represented.

uniform_spend(total, 5.5) gives 0.5/5.5 at year -5 and 1/5.5 at each of -4..0, six buckets. The last bucket sits at year 0 and earns no interest. Only REACTOR_CAP uses it. Licence, power island, capture, IHX, recycle train and the SMR island are single spends at year 0 (dcf.rs:250,252, with_replacement), so they have no construction profile. CONSTRUCTION_YEARS 5.5 is labelled INL NZW09 base case, uniform spend at 8%.

The DCF has no IDC line. At year 0 the reactor PV is capital x 1.20023, which is the bucket compounding at 8%. The ledger IDC line is capital x (f-1) x CRF with f = ((1+r)^N-1)/(rN) = 1.19766, a smooth extension to N = 5.5. They are identical at integer N. This 0.00257 difference is the whole 25 y gap. For BOAK 25 y, RC = 742.77 S$M predicts 0.3093 S$/t against 0.309322 in the CSV. L_economics.tex:48 admits it. The SMR island TCR already carries its own IDC (dcf.rs:9-12).

Replaced in full every 25 y, with the unused life of the last unit credited straight line at the horizon: SMR island (both plants), CAPTURE_CAP, IHX (k.ihx_life, 25 y at Central) and RECYCLE_TRAIN. At 60 y the flows fall at years 0, 25, 50 and a -0.6c credit at 60. Not replaced: reactor, power island, licence. DECOM is one flow at the horizon (dcf.rs:251). dcf.rs never reads k.decom_rate, so a High-level DCF would differ from the ledger's 3% sinking fund (economics.rs:344). Every caller uses central, so this is latent.

The discount rate is the Model field rate = DISCOUNT 0.08, real, 'project basis, same as IEAGHG'. It is not in CostQuery. CostQuery.r and CostItems.r_charged are reactor MWth, not a rate, which invites mistakes. The same rate discounts costs, H2 (dcf.rs:272-273) and abated tonnes, and sets IDC in the ledger.

LAC = (NPV_NUSH2 - NPV_SMR) x 1e6 / (a_atm x sum_{y=1..L} (1+r)^-y). LCOH = NPV x 1e6 / (NPV_H2 x 1000). Tonnes are constant from year 1 with no ramp-up. The abatement a_atm comes from emissions(), emissions.rs:45-58, and feeds both L5 (dcf.rs:278) and the DCF. There are 38 .a_atm uses in the repo, so the carbon-balance rebuild reaches the DCF through that one function.

The only stated tolerance is |gap_rel| <= 0.10 (LAC_GAP_LIMIT, eq L.37). LAC_DCF minus L5 at n = 1.0, 210 MWth, 25/40/60 y, in S$/t (share of L5): FOAK +0.49 (0.18%), +0.80 (0.32%), +0.49 (0.20%); BOAK +0.31 (0.16%), +0.64 (0.37%), +0.33 (0.20%); 10OAK_P47 +0.35 (0.17%), +0.67 (0.36%), +0.37 (0.20%); 10OAK_P46 +0.22 (0.15%), +0.56 (0.42%), +0.25 (0.20%). The largest of all 72 points is 0.47% (10OAK_P46, 40 y, charged at need). At 25 y the gap is all reactor IDC. At 40 and 60 y it adds CAPTURE_CAP, IHX and RECYCLE_TRAIN, from the replacement credit against a perpetual CRF.

The methods are independent only in timing. Both read cost_items, one rate and one tonnage, and the docs state that LAC equals AC at constant flows. The limit is about 20 times looser than any observed gap. A 2-3 S$/t timing error, or a 6% error from a mis-based grant, would pass. A shared error such as a wrong eligible base would leave the gap at zero.

The SMR island (IEAGHG TCR, FOM, water and chemicals), the gas, steam and power lines, and the reactor OCC (INL) are literature plant results copied in as cost inputs. They sit on both sides and cancel in LAC (test dcf.rs:498). They reach LCOH, which the LCOH_SOURCE note already flags (export.rs:3355).

The existing co-funding is rx_mult. It multiplies reactor capital inside cost_items, before IDC and CRF, so it acts as a pro-rata grant that also removes IDC on the granted share. cofunding_rows solves it by secant to TARGET_MATURE_COST 96 (not 100), only for BOAK at 25 and 60 y. It has no timing, no eligible set and no share grid. Do not reuse it as the grant.

Grant at close: one negative flow dated at the earliest point, -whole = -5 (the first bucket's date), for share x eligible nominal CAPEX. Its PV is G x 1.08^5, so the benefit includes interest saved. Progressive: -share x each uniform_spend bucket on the same dates. Both are NusH2 lines, so the NPV gap and LAC pick them up. Grant PV is 0.5 x RC x 1.08^5 against 0.5 x RC x 1.20023 for progressive.

items.finding: Keep IDC separate by taking the eligible base from nominal (undiscounted) spend and reporting IDC as PV minus the nominal sum of each line. In the ledger, IDC on the net-funded amount is: progressive (1-s) x IDC_gross; at close IDC_gross - G x ((1+r)^t_close - 1). If the close date is -5 in the DCF but N = 5.5 in the closed form, the 50% mismatch is about 2.4 to 5.5 S$/t (my estimate: G x (1.08^5.5 - 1.08^5), 1.2% to 2% of L5). The 0.10 limit would not flag it.

Grant wrongly applied to interest: (a) a base of capital x 1.2002 over-grants by 20%, worth 11.9 S$/t at 50% for BOAK 25 y, 6.3% of L5, and it would pass the 10% test because both methods share the base; (b) applying the share to a year-0 PV and also dating it at a negative year compounds it twice; (c) including the SMR TCR makes the state pay IDC that IEAGHG already embedded; (d) a grant line with no matching GapTerm breaks gap_terms_sum_to_the_gap (dcf.rs:485) and the REACTOR_CAP_WITH_IDC pairing.

The target is 'strictly below S$100/t' but TARGET_COST = 100 is solved to equality (tests assert |cost - target| < 1e-6, m9_economics.rs:159). 'Met' uses <= (wasm solve.rs:679, 864; frontend/app.js:404). LAC is affine in the grant share, so secant is exact. Report the infimum s*, which is the share at LAC = 100, and state LAC < 100 for every larger share. Preview for a reactor-only grant, my estimate from the CSV with a pro-rata IDC: s* is FOAK 25/60 y 0.77/0.71, BOAK 0.62/0.53, 10OAK_P47 0.67/0.59, 10OAK_P46 0.46/0.32. ae87df3d5d2f9884e.summary: The headline CO2 result is not built from the plant's own streams. It comes from an algebraic "anchored" carbon ledger (Model::carbon, anchored.rs:934-1030) tied to INL Case 6 numbers (34 MMSCFD gas, 1927 st/d captured, phi 0.775). That ledger feeds Model::emissions (emissions.rs:45) and from there the abatement, the cost ladder, the DCF, the exports and the wasm reply. A real stream-based Level 3 flowsheet exists (flowsheet.rs, FS_ runs) with a carbon ledger that closes to 5e-9 kmol C/h, but it only validates the anchored ledger and never drives a headline number. It disagrees with the anchor by 19.7 percent on the stack carbon (93.9 vs 116.9 kmol C/h) and fails its own gate FS_GATE_M7. Carbon closes in both ledgers by construction, so closure is a bookkeeping check and not evidence of capture performance. Missing carbon is typed as unknown only inside close_carbon; the live ledger cannot hold an unknown. No CO2e quantity exists anywhere in the engine. Source for numbers: results/Integrated_Mass_Balance.csv and results/Validation_Results.csv, plus the code lines cited.

items.where: flowsheet.rs:166-174 NG_MOL_FRACTIONS, :199-212 natural_gas; carbon.rs:72; flowsheet.rs:1635; parameters.toml C_PER_MOL_NG_*
items.finding: Natural gas feed is modelled from the published composition (TEV-953 A-5, TEV-961 A-50), lumped (C6 as 1.2 C5, O2 into N2), and is the only carbon input of CarbonLedger.closure. In the L3 run the gas rate is solved to the H2 basis (FS_B_REC_F 1212.25 kmol C/h). The anchored ledger instead fixes feed = NG_CASE6 x C_PER_MOL (anchored.rs:649), i.e. INL's 34 MMSCFD scaled by s_b (1219.23 kmol C/h).

Reformer outlet S05 and shift outlets S07 and S09 are calculated (equilibrium reformer, Case 5 shift chain, HTS bed sized on the IEAGHG approach). They are not separate lines of CarbonLedger (the ledger's tube field is S04, the reformer inlet), but each unit's element closure is tested at 1e-9 (m7_flowsheet.rs:31-45). Case 5 set temperatures and pressures are process assumptions, and the flowsheet gives phi = 0.8256 against the anchored 0.775.

items.where: flowsheet.rs:526-531 AnchoredMea::solve; parameters.toml:331 ETA_MEA; gates.rs:296-297; carbon.rs:75-80
items.finding: Absorber inlet S11, treated gas S12, CO2 S19 and storage CO2 S20 are modelled, and captured (S20) is a closure output. Captured CO2 is fixed as cap = ETA_MEA (0.90, author design value, decision D25) x S11 CO2, not computed by a column. The column models exist in nush2_units but gate M6 (T02) is recorded as Failed, so MEA capture is a specified input.

PSA reject S14 and recycle S03 are modelled, but the recycle share is f = about 0.752, taken from the anchored INL_SEL ledger (Case 6 captured 1927 st/d, Selexol 99 percent, PHI_RECYCLE 0.775). It is applied unchanged although the flowsheet's own phi differs, so this one copied number fixes the stack carbon, the recycle and the tail gas. Recycled and tail-gas carbon are internal and not in the closure outputs.

The nitrogen-rich cut S15 is modelled and is the plant's only atmospheric carbon outlet; ledger.burned is carbon of S15 and equals S16 stack carbon by complete combustion. Feed N2 leaves only in the cut (n2_cut, tested to 1e-9). Air N2 and excess air are not tracked.
H2 product carbon is CH4 only at 0.1 mol percent (published spec). CO and CO2 carry-over to the product are zero by construction, not computed. The size is 4.46 kmol C/h, 0.37 percent of feed.

Condensate CO2 is modelled by the flash drum (Henry, Aronu 2011 Eq 17): 5.28 kmol C/h in FS_B_REC_F, 0.44 percent of feed, and it is in the L3 closure. The anchored headline ledger has no condensate field and no such term in its closure; the CO2 is vented only in the S14 sensitivity (vent_condensate), so the headline captured figure includes it. Dissolved CH4, CO and H2 are held at zero by a stated assumption.

No stream exists for MEA make-up, degradation or slip (MEA carbon enters only the solvent element closure), for CO2 water and impurities or losses between S19 and S20 (S20 is pure CO2, 100 percent transferred), for transport and storage loss (only the TS_BURDEN 0.025 t/t ratio, author assumption, not verified), for steam or grid supply fuel, or for start-up and flaring. None is held as unknown: CarbonLedger fields are plain f64 and closure() always passes Some, so the None path of close_carbon is exercised only by unit tests. A missing stream would therefore fail the run (unreachable_stream) or be silently omitted, never carried as unknown.

plant_capture = captured/(captured + atm), reduction = a_atm/baseline and ci_kg_kg = atm/h2_t_y are all direct and capture based. The flowsheet's own plant capture (captured/feed, capture_pair) differs in denominator and is not exported.

items.finding: Provenance vocabulary is three closed lists. class: published, assumed, calculated, user_decision. rigour: rigorous, reduced_order, empirical, fixed_assumption, external_boundary. source_status: primary, via_reader, via_old_repo, not_verified. Required fields are id, value, unit, group, class, rigour, source, locator, source_status. Optional fields are low, high, decision (a D-number) and name. An unknown field, bad enum word, duplicate id or empty source or locator is a parse error. In use: 226 of 231 are fixed_assumption, via_old_repo is never used, 27 are not_verified.

A new parameter needs a [[param]] block, an r.get(...) in Model::build, and for a hard limit an entry in the LIMITS array (only 8 ids are limited today; low and high are never checked against value, and group is free text). If build never reads the id, the PARAMS_COMPLETE row in the validation harness fails. The browser needs a num(...) Spec in wasm registry.rs, whose hard and model ranges are enforced there. Final_Design_Basis.csv prints every registry entry automatically (export.rs:573-600, scope at export.rs:378).

DISCOUNT 0.08 (assumed, same as IEAGHG) is the single rate for CRF, the IDC factor and the DCF. CONSTRUCTION_YEARS 5.5 y (published, INL NZW09) is one value for every stage. There is no separate IDC rate, debt share or spend profile. Interest during construction is derived: (1+i)^T minus 1 over iT times reactor capital.

Maturity: FOAK_LOW/CENTRAL/HIGH 1.3/1.6/2.1 (published INL Table 1). BOAK is the literal 1.0 in stage_mult (economics.rs:202), not a parameter. LEARNING 0.1 per doubling and LEARNING_UNITS 10 give lf10 = 0.9^log2(10) = 0.7047. Stage ids: 10OAK_P46 is learning from BOAK (multiplier lf10), 10OAK_P47 is learning from FOAK (FOAK x lf10). Check: 2184 x lf10 = US$1,539/kWt and x 1.6 = 2,462, as the docs state.

Lives: LIVES_SHORT/MID/LONG 25/40/60 y (assumed, D08), ITEM_LIFE_Y 25 y for capture, IHX, recycle train and SMR island. Reactor REACTOR_RATED_MWTH 210 (user_decision D03). Size exponents N_LINEAR 1.0, N_TEAM 0.6, N_NGNP 0.3107 (computed at anchored.rs:613-619, not a registry id). Targets TARGET_ABATEMENT 250,000 t/y, TARGET_COST 100, TARGET_MATURE_COST 96 S$/t (user_decision). No horizon or life parameter is stage specific.

No subsidy, grant or eligibility parameter exists. The only grep hit, DECOM_FUND_RATE_HIGH (toml:2118), is a decommissioning trust return. A one-lever co-funding sweep exists: cofunding_rows solves CostQuery.rx_mult so BOAK, n = 1.0, 210 MWth reaches TARGET_MATURE_COST 96, giving 65.0% of S$742.77M at 25 y and 56.0% at 60 y on L5. It covers BOAK only, reactor capex only, with timing implicit (rx_mult scales capex before IDC). rx_mult is also the generic capex stress lever (vv/src/golden.rs:631, 642), so it should not become the grant field.

IDC is continuous in the ledger and discrete year buckets in the DCF. At BOAK 25 y the whole L5 to DCF gap of 0.3093 S$/t equals GAP_REACTOR_CAP_WITH_IDC (0.3093). At 60 y the IDC term is 0.2668 of a 0.3328 gap. Grant timing will move this gap, so the gap test needs its own tolerance statement.

Only reactor capital carries IDC in either method. Capture, IHX, licence, power island and recycle train enter at year 0 with no construction interest. An alternative eligible set that includes these items has no IDC to treat separately unless that is added to both methods.

Ranges are stored up to four times. GAS, TS, OCC, FOAK and OPEX _CENTRAL carry low and high equal to the separate _LOW and _HIGH ids (checked by script), and the browser registry holds its own hard and model ranges (gas hard 8 to 25 against engine 10 to 20). They can drift apart.
The DCF truncates item life and IHX life to u32 while the ledger uses real values. Only the High-level IHX life (105,120 h over 7,446 h = 14.1 y) differs, so the central baseline is unaffected.

Minor items. A test asserts more than 131 entries against 231 actual. The file header omits the optional name field, and N_TEAM's name embeds the value 0.6. GAS_CENTRAL 15.0 is 'published' but the cited arithmetic gives 14.97. BASELINE_IEAGHG_ROUNDED is read yet 'used by no result'. Two H2 normal densities exist (0.08988 not_verified, 0.08994).

Abatement is that baseline less the carbon burned in the INL-anchored Model::carbon split. These are copied plant results inside the abatement that item 1 must replace.

PHI_RECYCLE 0.775 is reconstructed from INL Case 5 stream tables (calculated). ETA_MEA 0.9 is an author design value (assumed). Capture capex per tonne uses IEAGHG Case 1A aMDEA on syngas (ΔTCR EUR41.02M at 46.6 t/h) as central and Case 3 MEA on flue gas as high, so the central cost is not MEA based, although the tonnage multiplied in is the plant's own.

ad5d97fc0494d4ae5.summary: Answers. (1) Partly yes. Headline abatement A = 578,052 t/y for B_REC_F is baseline 616,361 t/y minus 38,309 t/y to atmosphere (emissions.rs:46-57). The baseline is the INL TEV-953 conventional-SMR result (3205 st/d) scaled by H2 output, so an external plant result sets 93.8% of A. The atmosphere term is computed, but from an algebraic balance whose feed, H2 pair, recycle split and post-shift carbon split are all INL Case 5/6 numbers (anchored.rs:934-1030). (2) The "own balance, externals only bound it" description holds only for Cho 9.35 and IEAGHG 8.996 kg/kg; they bound A by +1.6% and -2.5%, and LAC_DCF_25 moves 190.1 to 187.0 or 194.9 S$/t. a07b8083510654136.summary: The browser simulator is a thin shell over one wasm reply. A registry call builds the controls, each change triggers a full solve, and every view reads only state.lastOk. Adding co-funding is mostly additive: new SPECS rows, a new block in cost_section, one new view. The real hazards are the self test, the CSV-to-reference build chain, the content guard, and the abatement labels the tour and charts hard-code. A 4 x 4 x 2 matrix is cheap next to the 109 cost_point calls a full solve already makes. A bisection-based break-even would not be. Nothing was built or run; timings below are from the README or inferred from code.

items.finding: The registry (cmd 1) loads once and sets the defaults. Each input change schedules a solve after 200 ms. rpc() posts {schema:1, inputs, kpi_only:false} to one worker, with one solve in flight, latest wins, and a 10 s timeout that restarts the worker. The reply JSON is parsed on the main thread into state.lastOk, and all views read that object only.

There are 22 controls: 8 enums (basis, tail_gas, heat_basis, stage, life_y, n, charged, occ_level) and 14 numbers. Only Number and Enum kinds exist, so a listed set of eligible items needs a named-set enum or a new Kind. controls.js builds groups, sliders, range text, flags, and the sweep and tornado lists from the registry alone, so a new SPECS row needs no JS.

Maturity is the stage enum: BOAK (default), FOAK, 10OAK_P46 (from BOAK), 10OAK_P47 (from FOAK). Life is 25 (default), 40 or 60 y. Discount defaults to 0.08 (hard 0.03 to 0.12). The others are n (1.0, 0.6, 0.31), charged (rating or required), occ_level, gas_s_gj, ts_s_t, capture_fom and availability. CONSTRUCTION_YEARS (5.5 y) is not exposed and no grant input exists.

A solve reply holds schema, engine, status, inputs, violations, flags, messages, kpi (32 ids, the first 24 required), kpi_class, feasibility, targets and engine_fields_missing. A full solve adds units (20), profiles, balances and cost{selected, ledger, ladder, grid, headline}, with streams null. Extra fields are safe. SCHEMA must stay 1 because other values are refused.

A full solve already calls cost_point about 109 times: 2 run() calls with 12 each, 12 in target_cases, 1 selected, and 72 in cost_section (2 charged x 4 stages x 3 lives x 3 n). A kpi_only solve makes about 37. cost.headline (72 rows) and cost.grid (432 rows) already hold L5 and DCF for all four maturity routes at every life.

A 4 x 4 x 2 matrix is 32 cost_points, and each returns L5 and DCF together. A DCF cell builds about 24 cash lines, roughly 14 of them annual vectors of 25 or 60 entries, using one powi per flow, and calls cost_items three times. Estimate: tens of microseconds per cell and 1 to a few ms for 32, against a measured 30 to 42 ms full solve. The cost sits in the DCF year vectors. Bisection for the break-even would add about 640 cost_points, six times today's load.

render() runs on every reply and calls the route hook registered by registerRoute. Each mount is rebuilt with replaceChildren, using section(), guard() and frame() plus one chart function. Every chart gets a Show table toggle, roving arrow-key focus and focus tooltips. dumbbell suits L5 against DCF, lineChart with ref suits LAC against subsidy share with the S$100/t line, and barChart suits break-even.

The cost table columns come from data/reference.json cost_headline, built from results CSV ids, and not from the reply. COST_ID uses [A-Z0-9]+ and cannot match 10OAK_P46, so the tenth-of-a-kind routes are silently absent from every table and from the headline parity check, although the reply carries them. A new comparison view should read res.cost directly.

The drawing needs res.units[id] for 20 [data-unit] groups, each with 7 filled sections, plus registry.units status. It also uses 9 data-bind paths (kpi.rating_mwth, q_process_mwth, h2_product_t_y, co2_captured_t_y, units.htgr/smr/power values, inputs.w_mea) and data/streams.json from the FS_B_REC_F flowsheet. Co-funding adds none of these, so the drawing is safe unless unit item ids change.

There are 13 steps and about 60 reply paths. The closing step reads kpi.abatement_t_y, abatement_cho_t_y, abatement_ieaghg_t_y, co2_atm_t_y, co2_captured_t_y, target_abatement_t_y, balances.carbon.baseline_t_y and targets.abatement.{met,at_or_above_target,feasible}. tourAudit fails any path that is neither finite nor a null listed in engine_fields_missing. The co2 step needs units.co2_storage.results.ts_cost (the TS ledger line).

The headline abatement is labelled INL baseline everywhere, and balances.carbon.baseline_t_y is the unabated SMR baseline, not a stream of this plant. The Cho and IEAGHG variants are also bounds from the literature. Rebuilding from the carbon balance means changing labels and prose in five places. The kpi ids should stay so the tour audit and the required-KPI block keep working.

About 34 checks run in headless Chrome: wasm parity against data/reference.json (rel 1e-6), Case A parity, MATURE_60Y parity, target_verdicts_agree, panels, charts_have_marks, visible_text_rules and 12 tour checks. CI runs desktop and --reduced-motion; the --mobile run is manual. The solve budget is 3000 ms in the test and 500 ms recorded for the first solve.

Each control is probed alone from defaults and must move one of the 24 required KPIs (the 24th is cost_s_per_t). Eligible-items and grant-timing controls are inert at 0 percent subsidy, and timing may only move DCF, which is not required. Both checks fail unless they probe with a nonzero grant or the grant folds into cost_s_per_t.

KPI_CELLS maps KPI ids to RES_* and cost row ids. RESULTS, EXPECTED and CSV_FILES each list the seven CSVs. scenario() raises BuildError if the MATURE_60Y rows or their note text are removed, which fails the whole site build. Any exporter renaming must be applied in all of these places.

The guard scans every file in _site, including data/*.json and csv, for withdrawn tokens: S$96, 106.5, 99.4, S$99.0, S$100.2, S$111.1, S$112.4, the word Achieved, and the em dash. One-decimal LAC or break-even values near 100 can hit these by chance. Use Met, not Achieved, and avoid SMR before it is defined.

The cost verdict uses <= against 100, and the strings and keys say at or below (at_or_below_target). The new goal is strictly below. Change the Rust comparisons and the text together. The self test compares .met flags only, so it will not catch a mismatch in wording.

Accessibility: skip link, role=status, focus-visible outlines, table alternatives, roving focus, and light mode only. The tour and PFD honour prefers-reduced-motion. The Results contents links use smooth scrolling unconditionally, and .viz-mark has a 120 ms transition outside the query. The dashboard mount is rebuilt on each solve and only the scenario radios restore focus, so new interactive controls belong in Parameters.

resultCsv flattens kpi, units, balances, cost.ledger, ladder, headline and targets by explicit loops. A new reply block exports nothing until a loop is added. inputsJson copies registry parameters automatically. buildPrint prints the costTable, a MATURE_60Y line and a hard-coded BOAK, 25 y description.
